# 01 Extract the shared timeline resolver

## Outcome

`resolveTimeline` is written once. `buildFlowchartModel` and `buildClassModel` call it, and their
behavior — every diagnostic, every message string, every dedupe tie-break — is byte-identical to
what they do today.

## Why this ticket exists

The function exists twice, near-verbatim: `buildFlowchartModel.ts:52` and
`buildClassModel.ts:733`. The only difference between them is cosmetic — one spells the
visible-before check `kind === "highlight" || kind === "exit" || kind === "unhighlight"`, the other
`kind !== "enter"`, over a four-verb union. Sequence would be the third copy.

The rules are already kind-agnostic: they consume a raw `SirenTimeline` and a set of valid ids and
never look at a node, a class or a participant. That is the same property that made
`parseTimelineBlock` shareable, and it is why this is an extraction rather than a redesign.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `packages/core/src/graph-model/resolveTimeline.ts` exports
      `resolveTimeline(timeline: SirenTimeline | null, validTargetIds: ReadonlySet<string>,
      diagnostics: Diagnostic[]): ResolvedTimeline`.
- [x] A `null` timeline returns `{ totalSteps: 0, entries: [] }` and pushes no diagnostics.
- [x] `buildFlowchartModel` and `buildClassModel` both call it; neither declares a local
      `resolveTimeline` any more.
- [x] `resolveTimeline.test.ts` covers the rules directly at the new seam: unknown id dropped with
      an error, `enter`/`exit` deduped to the earliest step with a warning (ties keeping the
      first-declared), a same-step tie, an action before its target's `enter` step rejected with an
      error, `totalSteps` as the maximum surviving step.
- [x] Every existing `buildGraphModel.test.ts` and `buildClassModel.test.ts` assertion about
      timeline diagnostics still passes **unedited** — this ticket changes no behavior, so a test
      that needed changing is a bug in the extraction.
- [x] The module carries a doc comment saying why it is shared (kind-agnostic inputs), naming
      `parseTimelineBlock` as the precedent.

## Test seam

`resolveTimeline` directly, plus the two existing model test files as the regression net.

## Write ownership

- `packages/core/src/graph-model/resolveTimeline.ts` (new)
- `packages/core/src/graph-model/resolveTimeline.test.ts` (new)
- `packages/core/src/graph-model/buildFlowchartModel.ts`
- `packages/core/src/graph-model/buildClassModel.ts`

Do **not** touch `contracts.ts` — every type this needs is already exported.
